entries.title: Mark 6:1
segments: His own country. His second visit to Nazareth.  He was treated in the same manner on his first visit (
).  There is no record of his ever having been in Nazareth again.

entries.title: Mark 6:3
segments: Is not this the carpenter, etc.  The description of our Lord as 'the carpenter' is peculiar to Mark.  In Matthew he is spoken of as 'the carpenter's son' (
).  There is an old tradition that Jesus made yokes and ploughs.

entries.title: Mark 6:7
segments: Authority over the unclean spirits. To that extent he imparted to his disciples his power of working miracles.

entries.title: Mark 6:8
segments: Wallet. Made of leather to contain food, and carried over the shoulder.

entries.title: Mark 6:9
segments: Sandals. Made of bark, usually of the palm tree.

entries.title: Mark 6:10
segments: Wheresoever ye enter. They were to abide in the house which received them.  Matthew adds that they were to salute it (

segments: Shake off the dust that is under your feet. This was to be a witness against those who rejected Christ.  See note on
.  Paul did this on two notable occasions.  See

entries.title: Mark 6:14
segments: King Herod. Herod Antipas, tetrarch of Iturea and Perea.  He was the son of Herod the Great.

entries.title: Mark 6:16
segments: John, whom I beheaded, he is risen. Superstition and remorse led Herod to believe that the man whom he had murdered had risen from the dead.  As a thoroughgoing Sadducee in his sympathy Herod did not believe in the resurrection, but his troubled conscience overcame his disbelief.

entries.title: Mark 6:17
segments: For the sake of Herodias. See note on

entries.title: Mark 6:22
segments: Daughter of Herodias. Salome.  See note on

entries.title: Mark 6:24
segments: What shall I ask? This was the opportunity for revenge that Herodias longed for.  See notes on

entries.title: Mark 6:26
segments: The king was exceeding sorry. A proof of his high regard for John.  Though depraved himself, he recognized the strength and loftiness of the prophet's character.  See note on

entries.title: Mark 6:27
segments: In the prison. At Machaerus, where a fort and prison had been built.  It was about five miles east of the Dead Sea.

entries.title: Mark 6:30
segments: And the apostles gather themselves together. This was their return to Capernaum to tell the Master about the results of their first mission.

entries.title: Mark 6:31
segments: No leisure so much as to eat. Besides those assembled to hear our Lord and to be healed, Capernaum was now crowded with pilgrims on their way to the Passover feast at Jerusalem (
).  From the excessive toil thus caused Jesus called the apostles to rest themselves.

entries.title: Mark 6:32
segments: To a desert place apart. Near Bethsaida Julias, a few miles northeast of the Sea of Galilee.  This town was originally called Bethsaida.  It had been greatly improved and enlarged by the tetrarch Herod Philip, who gave it the additional name of Julias in honor of the daughter of the Roman emperor.

entries.title: Mark 6:35
segments: The place is desert. It was probably uninhabited, but not all sandy waste.  See

segments: Five, and two fishes. They found that a lad had five barley loaves and two small fishes (

entries.title: Mark 6:40
segments: In ranks. In groups.

entries.title: Mark 6:44
segments: Were five thousand men. Matthew says, 'about five thousand men, besides women and children.'  See note on
.  According to custom the women and children would stand or sit separate from the men.

entries.title: Mark 6:45
segments: And straightway he constrained his disciples. No time was to be lost in preventing the multitude, who were astounded by this miracle, from forcibly attempting to make him king.  See

.  Therefore he sent the disciples by boat across the lake while he dispersed the people.

segments:
The fourth watch. Three o'clock in the morning.
 

 
Walking on the sea. Like the feeding of the five thousand, this miracle was a direct mastery of the powers of nature.

entries.title: Mark 6:53
segments: The land unto Gennesaret. On the northwestern shore of the Sea of Galilee.  It is a plain, three miles long by one wide and remarkable fertile.
